title: Optimizing Garbage Collection Latency with Generational ZGC
explanation: Generational Z Garbage Collector transforms Java memory management by applying the weak generational hypothesis to a concurrent, region-based collector. Traditional low-latency collectors struggle with the overhead of tracking object age across large heaps. Generational ZGC maintains separate generations for young and old objects, automatically capturing generational changes concurrently without stopping application threads. This matters because it dramatically reduces CPU overhead and allocation stalls for memory-intensive enterprise applications. By focusing collection efforts primarily on short-lived objects, it achieves sub-millisecond pause times even across multi-terabyte heaps.
takeaway: Adopting generational concurrent collectors eliminates the traditional trade-off between massive heap capacity and predictable low-latency performance in high-throughput enterprise systems.
